title: Consumer Rights Act 2015 — goods remedies spine

sections.label: CRA s.9 — satisfactory quality
sections.summary: Goods supplied by a trader must be of satisfactory quality.

sections.label: CRA s.10 — fitness for particular purpose
sections.summary: Goods must be fit for a particular purpose made known to the trader.

sections.label: CRA s.19 — rights to enforce terms about goods
sections.summary: Sets out short-term reject, repair/replacement, and price reduction / final reject. Within 6 months of delivery, a lack of conformity is generally treated as present on delivery unless the trader proves otherwise.

sections.label: CRA s.20 — right to reject
sections.summary: Right to reject non-conforming goods and treat the contract as at an end (subject to the Act).

sections.label: CRA s.22 — short-term right to reject (30 days)
sections.summary: Short-term reject time limit is usually 30 days from delivery. Asking for repair/replacement can pause that clock while you wait.

sections.label: CRA s.23 — repair or replacement
sections.summary: Consumer may require repair or replacement within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience.

sections.label: CRA s.24 — price reduction or final right to reject
sections.summary: After one failed repair/replacement (or repair not done in time), consumer may choose price reduction or final reject. Use deduction may apply on final reject; for motor vehicles the usual first-6-months bar on use deduction does not apply (s.24(10)).
